decisions.reason: Uses console-excerpt.txt and both slots-contract excerpts to name plugin A as the only crash: its unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call throws TypeError at render because alpha.2 SessionStandardProps dropped that seat in favor of useSessionStatus, while useSessions and useProjection survive (does not claim useSessions was removed). Correctly states plugin B renders no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing, treating the two symptoms as one coupled breakage.

Explains via dock-render-tree.md that conversation.input.dock is one list slot whose entries mount under a single shared DrawerErrorBoundary with null fallback and no per-entry boundary, so plugin A's throw unmounts the whole subtree including B's chips entry; the attach button survives because conversation.input.left is a different slot under its own boundary. Backs this with the boundary-fallback console follow-up naming both unmounted entries.

Reads tried-notes.txt correctly: disabling A restoring B's chips proves A's crash caused the unmount and B renders once freed; explicitly states it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible elsewhere nor that A's crash is the only dock defect; explains reinstalling B could never help because B was never broken; rejects the colleague's both-plugins theory since B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Corrected component code reads pending state through useSessionStatus (mapping pendingInteraction) when supplied, falls back to useSessionPendingInteraction on alpha.1, and with neither degrades silently via typeof-function guards and empty-map fallbacks, so only pending indicators hide while running/todos/token/ETA keep working. Explains silence is required because a throwing dock tenant unmounts co-tenants — cosmetic loss versus multi-plugin outage.

Verification avoids host restart by patching plugin A's client bundle and letting the web client refresh/HMR re-fetch it, checks both dock entries render together with console free of the TypeError and boundary fallback, and covers B regression (paste/add/remove/re-paste, negative control with A disabled). Hygiene: tenants destructure defensively, wrap their own entry in a local boundary, and the host could mount per-entry boundaries at the cost of nesting/layout complexity and quieter partial failures.

caps.reason: The final remedy fixes only plugin A's component code; the report explicitly shows plugin B was never broken (its reinstall could not help) and that the two symptoms are one shared-boundary coupling, not independent plugin-level bugs requiring parallel fixes.
